brief: A compact desk unit with a drawer, plus a spike at a corner where three bases meet to hold a small platform.

requirements.evidence: L-shaped cluster of 3 full bases (0,0,0; 1,0,0; 0,1,0) with top covers on 0,1,0, 1,0,0 and 0,0,1 providing flat desk surfaces; piece:0,0,1 stacked on 0,0,0 for height variation
Drawer frame notch installed at 1,-1 k4 (hex-drawer-frame-notch-mf) set open, but no drawer box/insert was confirmed via find_sockets and not placed - frame empty

requirements.requirement: Spike at corner where three bases meet
requirements.evidence: spike:0#0,0|0,1|1,0 placed at junction 0,0|0,1|1,0 where three bases meet (find_sockets confirmed junction)
Current spike is solid variant; configurator rejected setSpikeAccessory platform-sm with TYPE_NOT_ALLOWED - only mount spike can carry platform. Mount variant not installed before time expired

finish.summary: Compact L-shaped desk built with drawer frame and central spike; drawer remains frame-only and platform not mounted due to spike variant mismatch and time limit.

lines.label: M3 x 10 socket head screw, ISO 4762
M6 x 20 socket head screw, ISO 4762

notes: Tighten every M6 to 2 N.m: HAND TOOLS ONLY, never a cordless driver. These bolts clamp printed PETG, not metal: at the bolt's own 10.4 N.m rating the head crushes the plastic under it and the joint fails silently, looking tight while holding nothing. Snug, then a nudge. Re-check the bolts after the first few weeks: PETG relaxes under load and the clamp will have eased.
